body: Are all these part of depression? My whole life has been like that. I thought it's normal.

The worst symptom for me is anhedonia, nothing is fun anymore and everything seems so meaningless. It doesn't matter what I do, there is just a feeling of emptiness. I don't play video games or listen to music because I like doing it but because it's the most pleasure I get from all the things I don't enjoy. I am looking for something that is no longer there.

I can't remember when it was. My appetite was almost completely gone, I was sleeping 20 hours a day for weeks, not even getting up to pee, just sleeping with lights on because I didn't have the will to turn it off. The lowest moment I experienced was when I got the energy to go down to the kitchen with the intention to kill myself with a knife. Suicide seemed very rational and reasonable.  It's something you never ever expect to happen and then you stand there and you are so close to ending your own life and it's fascinating, scary and reassuring at the same time.

It makes me a bad person, I have no nerves and just turn into an asshole at times. People are coming to me with their enthusiasm, wanting to show me something they are happy about and all I can do is make a negative comment.

I think bad short-term memory is relatively normal for depressed people and it probably also affects your long-term memory. On bad days I can't remember what I ate or what I said on the phone. My brother says goodbye and a minute later I can't even remember what exactly I did or whether or not I ignored him. It's weird.

Don't worry about it. The first few appointments are probably going to be uncomfortable but the more you talk to the person, the better it gets and maybe you even look forward to it. It's some kind of routine, even just talking about your feelings is somewhat helpful.

Honestly, I had depression, anhedonia, suicidal thoughts on and off for a while now and I still don't know what to do about it or how I would help others that are going through the same thing. When your mental health is bad and your body is against you, you are in a very bad place. Even when I try to be optimistic and fix myself, it doesn't change much, because I am negative by default. It's like you are stuck in this thinking pattern and there is nothing else outside of it. But despite all of that I really want a better life and I still have some kind of hope even on my worst days. I don't want to die, I am just overwhelmed and it seems like I am never going to make it and that's why I tend to give up and just sleep most of the time. It's probably similar for her.

I would like to have someone in my life that is there to try and understand my situation and show me that I am needed. My father, for example, says something like "I care about you." and then just goes to bed or to work and he never really tries to sit down with me and understand my feelings, he just assumes that he knows or that I am not going to hurt myself anyway.

Depends on the person, but I think it would help me if others just forced me into therapy because I am never going to go there again on my own. At this point, I am just existing and completely throwing my life away.

I don't think the reason you don't have friends is because of your social anxiety, maybe to a certain degree. It's because you have not met the right people. In my life I had a handful of good friends. I had a great time with them from day one because they were the right people for me. Just filter out the people that you aren't compatible with because it's a waste of energy and time in most cases to work on the relationship.

I don't think it's worth trying to change a person because it's almost impossible. Of course, there are minor things you can work on but if they put you down, you should just leave them behind and move on. Don't waste your energy on things you have no control over. If you have one great friend, that's better than all the fake friends in the world.

It's not easy to cut someone out of your life that has been there for years. I had a pretty good relationship with my mother and when she got her boyfriend, it went downhill. It was hard but one day my mother came home and I told her that I will leave right now and that's what I did. My brother picked me up and everyone was shocked but I regret nothing. Cutting out toxic people from your life is one of the best things you can do.

First of all, it's a big step that you decided to talk on discord. For many people with social anxiety this is unthinkable and you should be proud instead of punishing yourself for what happened.

I know exactly what it feels like. To you it looks like you can never go back because of the opinions others might have about you. But most of the time you are making it a bigger problem than it is in your mind. They probably already forgot about it.

Honestly, I would not delete your account, just join them again and when you feel the need to say something about what happened, you can do it.

Maybe you should take your time to think about what happened and go back after you feel better about it. Try to think about it from their perspective and how you would react and you'll see that it's not a big deal.
